In this assignment, you'll be picking up where you left off with the M&Ms activity. You'll load the data and perform some basic statistical analysis. Follow the steps below to complete the assignment.

### Task 1: Load the tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```


### Task 2: Load the M&Ms dataset from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv
```{r}
mandms <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/mandms.csv")
```

### Task 3: Sample 5 rows of data from the dataset
```{r}
set.seed(42)
sample_5 <- mandms |> sample_n(5)
```


### Task 4: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the sample, using either the red or black number of M&Ms
```{r}
sample_5 |> 
summarize(mean_sample = mean(red), sd_sample = sd(red))
```


### Task 5: Calculate the mean age and standard deviation of the population, using the same measure as in Task 4
```{r}
mandms |>
summarize(mean_population = mean(red), sd_population = sd(red))
```



### Task 6: Compare the sample and population statistics

Compare the two sets of means and standard deviations. Are they similar?

These sets are pretty similar. I'm not surprised that the larger standard deviation number is from the population data because a larger size would naturally have more variability than the smaller sample size. 

### Task 7: Describe the results

Write a few sentences about what you found in the data. What does this tell you about the M&Ms dataset and about the act of random sampling?

This data shows that random sampling is a good way to find a mean that can reasonably represent a population. Using the standard deviation from the sample is less accurate to the actual standard deviation in the population because a smaller group will have less variability than the entire population. This particular sample doesn't show the entire spread of the population, as seen with the standard deviation. Just like we saw with the in-class experiment, random sampling consistently gave us means that were near the actual population mean, so random sampling is an effective way to get estimates of means and standard deviations.
